title: Stuck with the wrong plant

readouts.l: Average cost at this output (short run)
Long-run average cost at this output

predict.q: A firm makes 40 units a week in the plant built for 40 units. Demand rises for good, and it now makes 80. What happens to its average cost?

options.s: It falls at once, because a bigger output brings economies of scale
options.fb: Economies of scale are long run. With the old plant the firm moves up its SRAC: 5 → 7.

options.s: It rises at first, then falls below its old level once a bigger plant is built
options.fb: With the old plant, AC climbs 5 → 7. With a plant built for 80, it falls to 4.

options.s: It rises in the short run and in the long run, because of diminishing returns
options.fb: Diminishing returns hold only while the plant is fixed. With a plant built for 80, AC falls to 4.

options.s: It stays the same, because costs rise in proportion to output
options.fb: Average cost changes along both curves. Watch the point: 5, then 7, then 4.

task: Move the **output** slider from 40 to 80 and watch the point climb the old plant's SRAC. Then move the **plant size** slider to 80.

target.do: Set output to 80, then plant size to 80, then press Check.

takeaway: In the short run the firm moves along its SRAC; in the long run it changes plant and moves along the LRAC.
